transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-25
Time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~35 minutes
Attendees: Jared Klein (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Rao (Redwood CSM), Olivia Chen (CTO), Markus Vogel (Platform), Priya Singh (Security), Ethan Park (SRE)

Summary:
Quick sync on the VPC pilot: routing issues observed last week, attempted NAT fix, KV cache warmup variability, plan for a dry-run upgrade and more detailed network captures. Agreed next steps and owners.

00:00 Jared: okay everyone thanks for joining, uh quick check in for the weekly POC, can we do a 35 minute run, I know folks are heads down
00:12 Olivia: yes that works for us, thanks Jared
00:17 Maya: agenda — networking status, perf numbers since the last change, tuning notes, and then next steps for the upgrade window
00:28 Markus: quick note, we saw intermittent 500s hitting the private control plane when we routed through our transit gateway, not all requests just a subset, so we tried to add a specific route and also changed NAT behavior on the private subnets
00:45 Maya: got it, did you collect traceroute or tcpdump around the time of the errors? that helps diagnose if it's a routing blackhole vs MTU or connection reset
00:52 Markus: we ran traceroutes, i put a gist in the shared folder but i'll attach the route table dump after the call, there was one hop that timed out intermittently
01:07 Ethan: and to add, when the 500s happened token latency spiked to about 1.6s per token on average for the short chat tests which is higher than the baseline we saw earlier
01:22 Maya: hmm that aligns with connection retries at the transport layer; sometimes the runtime is waiting on tcp handshake and that amplifies per-token latency, especially with batching sizes of 8 we saw worse tail latency
01:40 Olivia: do you think this is an infra routing problem or something on your side with how the control plane talks to private pods?
01:48 Samir: from what we can tell it's mostly transit/VPC path instability; the control plane calls are idempotent and we have retries but they surface as backend errors if the path is flaky
02:03 Priya: security question — we need to confirm KMS usage for keys in the private deployment and whether auto-rotation will be supported — also audit logs retention for 90 days is a must for our compliance team
02:14 Jared: yes on KMS, the private package supports customer-managed KMS/HSM, we'll share the integration doc. auto-rotation is supported with our recommended rotation cadence, we'll call that out in the doc for Priya
02:28 Priya: great, also SAML provisioning and RBAC mapping — we need examples for groups and service accounts so we can map to our Okta directory
02:37 Maya: we'll include an RBAC example and a sample SAML assertion mapping, there are a few env names that the generator mislabels sometimes in our docs so we'll make it explicit
02:51 Markus: after the NAT change we saw fewer 502s but still a higher token latency for edge cases; I can walk through the timeline — we pushed the route change at 03:12 UTC and errors dropped but latency stayed elevated for about 20 minutes
03:09 Maya: that's useful. can you share the exact request ids? we can correlate with the control plane logs. Also, can you confirm whether the KV cache was warm for those tests?
03:20 Ethan: for the short chat tests the KV cache was only partially warm, we were running parallel workloads and cache hit rate was around 60% during the incident window
03:33 Maya: partial warm cache with intermittent routing errors explains tail latency. if the cache is cold we go further into the model compute path and coupled with retries you get spikes
03:46 Jared: tuning idea — decrease max batch size temporarily and increase request priority for interactive routes until the routing is stable. Maya, can you estimate the perf delta?
03:55 Maya: yeah, for interactive loads lowering batch to 4 from 8 reduced tail by about 18% in our lab; but cost goes up so it's a temporary mitigation while routing is fixed. Also, enabling prefix caching on the client side helped some teams earlier, it shaves off about 0.2s median when hit rates are decent
04:18 Olivia: cost is a concern but availability matters more for the pilot so we're okay to accept higher unit cost short term while we stabilize
04:26 Priya: for SOC 2 we need proof the data path doesn't persist customer prompt text beyond ephemeral caches and that control plane logs are encrypted at rest with CMKs; is that covered?
04:37 Jared: yes, control plane logs are written to encrypted buckets with CMK support; we'll surface the evidence and screenshots in the security pack. related - we do not persist raw prompt text in long-term storage by default in the private deployment
04:49 Priya: ok thanks, that should cover initial concerns; we'll carve out follow ups in the security doc review
04:56 Maya: next on upgrades — we have a minor runtime patch that addresses a keepalive/tcp timeout regression. we recommend a dry-run upgrade during low traffic, we'll need a 45 minute window with a 15 minute rollback guardrail
05:12 Markus: does the patch require node restarts or rolling restart? we need to schedule with our infra maintenance window and coordinate with our cloud provider regarding route propagation delays
05:21 Maya: it's rolling restarts of the inference pods, control plane remains up; we do drain + restart sequence per availability zone. time to drain depends on tail requests but usually under 3 minutes per AZ in our tests
05:35 Ethan: any known issues with the drain and active KV cache eviction? we rely on cache for latency and don't want a big cold start penalty
05:44 Maya: good question — our draining keeps KV cache in memory until instance shutdown; however if a pod is removed and replaced the new pod will need cache warmup. to reduce impact we propose staged drains and keep some instances healthy to serve cached requests
05:58 Jared: propose dry-run on 2026-12-02 02:00 UTC, Maya will run the upgrade, Markus and Ethan observe, Samir to coordinate rollback if needed. does that work?
06:09 Markus: should be fine subject to we finalize the precise maintenance window with our infra team
06:16 Priya: security will be on call to confirm audit trace during the run
06:21 Jared: perfect. on metrics, since last week we measured average token latency 0.9s and 95th at 1.6s for the interactive workload, after the NAT fix median improved to 0.8s but the tail stayed high during cache warm periods
06:39 Maya: we also collected a sample trace and attached a lightweight flamegraph in the shared folder — it's labelled flames-20261124.svg — it shows time spent in model compute vs preproc when cache misses occur
06:52 Olivia: i saw the flamegraph, useful to convince execs this is not model regression but infra. will you include an executive one-pager? we want a short note for leadership
07:03 Jared: yes we'll put together a one-pager summary and highlight mitigations and the planned dry-run date
07:12 Maya: tuning notes I'll share after correlating the traceroutes with the control plane logs, expect an email with the KV cache thresholds and suggested batch changes
07:20 Markus: also, can you include recommended route TTLs and any specific SG/NACL entries? last time the docs had an example but it didn't match our transit gateway setup exactly
07:31 Jared: we'll tailor the network examples to your transit gateway topology and include explicit route table entries and security group snippets
07:39 Samir: quick reminder — we'll need to collect post-upgrade logs and token-level cost delta so we can validate no regression; Samir will add a small dashboard in Redwood Console for the pilot metrics
07:52 Samir: I'll add the dashboard and set retention to 30 days for easy triage
07:58 Olivia: okay final check, anything else?
08:01 Priya: nothing else from security, thanks
08:03 Ethan: no, we'll run the tests and ping the team with traces
08:06 Jared: great thanks everyone. recap - dry-run upgrade 2026-12-02, network captures and traceroutes due by 11/30, security doc review by 12/03, tuning notes by 11/29. we'll follow up with calendar invites and file shares.
08:22 Jared: thanks all, bye
08:25 Olivia: bye
